html:
The Kingdom of Naples covered the whole of mainland southern Italy, from the Papal States to the heel and toe, with its capital at Naples. It existed as a separate kingdom from 1282 to 1816. The map shows it from 1530 to 1715, when Spain ruled it.

It split off from the Norman and Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily after the Sicilian Vespers of 1282, when the island went to Aragon and the mainland stayed with Charles of Anjou and his heirs. Alfonso V of Aragon conquered it in 1442. The French invasion of 1494 began the Italian Wars, and by 1504 Spain had won it.

For two centuries Spanish viceroys ruled. Naples grew into one of the largest cities in Europe. Heavy taxes provoked the revolt of Masaniello in 1647, and plague in 1656 killed a large part of the city. After the War of the Spanish Succession Austria held the kingdom from 1707, until a Spanish Bourbon prince, Charles, took it in 1734 and ruled it as an independent king. In 1816 it was merged with Sicily as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
